guide.telegram.blurb: Send a message to your bot from Telegram on your phone and Pageboy wakes up.
guide.telegram.what: No public website address needed: Pageboy periodically asks Telegram's servers “any new messages?”.
guide.telegram.steps: Open the Telegram app and search for BotFather.
Send /newbot and follow the prompts to pick a bot name and username.
Copy the long token BotFather sends you (a single line that looks like a password).
Paste it below, save, then press “Turn this channel on”.
guide.telegram.bot_token.label: Bot token
guide.telegram.bot_token.tooltip: The line BotFather sends right after /newbot. It looks like digits:letters — never share it with anyone.
guide.telegram.allowlist.label: Allowed chat / user IDs (optional · allowlist)
guide.telegram.allowlist.tooltip: Save numeric IDs separated by commas and only messages from that chat.id or sender user id (from.id) are handled; everything else is ignored. Note: allowing a group chat.id (negative) allows every member of that chat.
guide.telegram.allowlist.help: Save empty to clear (allow everyone) · comma-separated (note: a group chat.id allows everyone in it)
guide.slack.blurb: Send a message to your app/bot in a Slack workspace and Pageboy wakes up.
guide.slack.what: No public URL needed: Slack pushes events over a socket (Socket Mode) to this PC. Two keys are required.
guide.slack.steps: Create a new app with the “Create a Slack app” link below (choose your workspace).
Turn Socket Mode ON in the app settings.
Create an App-level Token with the connections:write scope and copy the xapp-… value.
Install the bot to your workspace via OAuth and copy the Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-…).
Subscribe to message events (e.g. message.channels / message.im).
Paste both values below, save, then press “Turn this channel on”.
guide.slack.bot_token.label: Bot token (xoxb-…)
guide.slack.bot_token.tooltip: The Bot User OAuth Token on the OAuth & Permissions page. It usually starts with xoxb- and needs the chat:write scope.
guide.slack.bot_token.help: Bot User OAuth Token — starts with xoxb-
guide.slack.app_token.label: App token (xapp-…)
guide.slack.app_token.tooltip: Create it under Basic Information → App-Level Tokens. It is for Socket Mode and needs connections:write. Starts with xapp-.
guide.jira.title: Jira / Confluence (reference)
guide.jira.blurb: This is not a “wake-up channel”. It is the surface your hook's program uses to read and write issues over REST when it needs to.
guide.jira.what: Unlike Telegram/Slack, Pageboy does not poll Jira. Instead, the scripts or agent CLIs you put in a hook call the Atlassian API.
guide.jira.steps: Sign in to your Atlassian account.
Under Security → API tokens, create a token with Create API token.
Give that token to your hook's exec program — not to a Pageboy channel — via an environment variable or the “Harness secret storage” below.
No public webhook URL is needed on this Alpha path.
guide.jira.note: To be clear: “a program launched by a hook” means a subprocess of the exec command registered on the hook. Pageboy does not ship a built-in Jira bot.
guide.app.title: Connect my Telegram account (browse chats · export)
guide.app.blurb: Pull the chat list, messages and files your account can see with pboy telegram … commands. Separate from the bot token (wake-up) and does not run hooks.
guide.app.api_id.tooltip: The api_id from my.telegram.org → API development tools. Digits only; not the BotFather bot token.
guide.app.api_id.help: Digits only · not the bot token
guide.app.api_hash.tooltip: The hash issued together with api_id on the same page. Save both to continue to phone verification.
guide.harness.jira_token.label: Jira API token (optional)
guide.harness.jira_token.tooltip: Your Atlassian API token. It is only stored and never shown again. Wiring it into a hook program may be a separate step.
guide.harness.jira_token.help: Unrelated to channel enable — a vault for harness/scripts
guide.harness.jira_email.label: Jira account email (optional)
guide.harness.jira_email.tooltip: The Atlassian account email used for Cloud REST Basic auth. Usually paired with the API token.
guide.harness.jira_email.help: Login email used together with the API token
